summary.oneLiner: Aditya Vision successfully pivoted from a H1-heavy seasonal model to an all-weather performer, delivering 28% Q4 revenue growth despite a weak summer, driven by strategic inventory stocking ahead of OEM price hikes and accelerated expansion in Uttar Pradesh. The shift in product mix toward higher-ASP but lower-margin mobiles/laptops compressed reported margins, masking the underlying operating leverage maturing stores will provide in FY27.
summary.business: Incorporated in 1999 at Patna, the Company operates a brick-and-mortar, multi-brand retail chain selling televisions, air conditioners, refrigerators and washing machines, digital gadgets such as mobile phones and laptops, and personal care and kitchen appliances, to customers in urban centres and emerging Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets of the Hindi Heartland. As on March 31, 2026 it ran 207 stores with an average store size of 4,400+ sq. ft. and a retail footprint of ~9.1 lakh sq. ft. across Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. Retail trade of electronic products contributes 98.06% of turnover; customers are B2B and B2C, exports are nil, and the Company is not engaged in any production or manufacturing activity.

currentContext.expansion: Expansion for Aditya Vision is store roll-out, not plant capex. During FY26 the Company opened 32 new stores across four states — 6 in Bihar, 4 in Jharkhand, 19 in Uttar Pradesh and 3 in Chhattisgarh — crossing the milestone of 200 operational stores through focused, cluster-led expansion. As on March 31, 2026 the store count stands at 207: Bihar 118 (all 38 districts), Jharkhand 33 (22 of 24 districts), Uttar Pradesh 53 (30 of 75 districts) and Chhattisgarh 3 (2 of 33 districts); retail footprint rose 22% to 9,13,725 sq. ft. with an average store size of 4,400+ sq. ft. Under 'Strategic Growth Pillars and Future Outlook' the Company states it plans to add at least 25–30 stores annually over the next 2–3 years on the base of 207 stores, anchored in sustaining strong double-digit same-store sales growth. It is focused on deepening presence across Bihar, Jharkhand, Eastern, Central and Western Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, and on entering Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal in the current calendar year, targeting underpenetrated markets. Operations run on a cash-and-carry model with 100+ brand partnerships and real-time API integration enabling rapid replenishment; consumer-finance tie-ups include Bajaj Finserv, HDB Financial Services, IDFC First Bank, Paytm, Pine Labs, Samsung Finance+ and TVS Credit. The annual report states no rupee capex quantum for this expansion, and BRSR Principle 2 reports nil R&D and nil capex in technologies to improve environmental and social impacts in both the current and previous financial year.

risks.note: MD&A: the Company may face disruption in business operations in the event of non-compliance with new policies or changes in existing policies; it mitigates by monitoring policy changes, engaging policymakers and diversifying markets.

MD&A: lucrative growth prospects of the industry lead to heightened competitive intensity from regional and national players; the Company relies on brand equity, product offering, service, reach and customer centricity as its edge.

MD&A: seasonality causes fluctuations in consumer demand that may lead to inventory imbalances and revenue volatility; managed via demand forecasting and season-based promotions. FY26 demonstrated this — an extended monsoon and one of the weakest summers in decades weighed on cooling-led demand in Q1 FY26.

MD&A: smooth supply chains are imperative for timely procurement at competitive prices; disruption may raise cost, cause delays and reduce profitability and brand equity. Mitigated through a network of channel partners (the disclosure is cut off mid-sentence in the report text supplied).

BRSR Section A: operations are in only four states (Bihar 118, Jharkhand 33, Uttar Pradesh 53, Chattisgarh 3 showrooms; 207 total), with retail trade of electronic products accounting for 98.06% of turnover and exports nil — leaving performance tied to Hindi Heartland consumption and, disproportionately, to Bihar.

risks.risk: Commodity pricing, chip shortage and global supply disruption
risks.note: MD&A industry overview: the consumer durables sector faces volatility in commodity pricing, an acute shortage of chips, and impact on both demand and supply from the ongoing Middle East crisis; GDP growth for FY27 is projected to decline to 6.9% with the Middle East conflict a key downside risk.

one-line thesis: Aditya Vision successfully pivoted from a H1-heavy seasonal model to an all-weather performer, delivering 28% Q4 revenue growth despite a weak summer, driven by strategic inventory stocking ahead of OEM price hikes and accelerated expansion in Uttar Pradesh. The shift in product mix toward higher-ASP but lower-margin mobiles/laptops compressed reported margins, masking the underlying operating leverage maturing stores will provide in FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 625cr (Q4, +28% YoY), INR 2,672cr (FY26, +18% YoY); EBITDA: INR 51cr (Q4, margin 8.1%), INR 228cr (FY26, margin 8.5%); PAT: INR 22cr (Q4, +36% YoY), INR 117cr (FY26, +11% YoY); Order Book: N/A (Retail); Net Debt: Not explicitly disclosed, but management confirms internal accruals + working capital borrowings suffice for capex, no equity raise planned. One-offs/Distortions: Margin compression due to mix shift (Mobile ASP +20%, Laptop ASP +8-10%) rather than operational inefficiency; Elevated 'other expenses' due to new brand ambassador (Pankaj Tripathi) and UP expansion costs.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Continuing robust trajectory (April described as 'very robust'); Margin: Target range 8%-10% (striving for 9%); Order Inflow: N/A; Capex/Commissioning: ~25-30+ new stores annually (calibrated cluster approach), focusing on UP, Chhattisgarh, and entry into Madhya Pradesh.
order book & pipeline: N/A - Retail business model relies on inventory turnover rather than order book. Inventory held at INR 840cr (strategically high) to secure pre-hike pricing and ensure availability for strong summer demand.
segment / subsidiary detail: Cooling (AC/Coolers/Fridges): Margin dilution in H1 due to weak summer, expected recovery in H2/FY27. Mobile/Laptops: Volume surge with significant ASP inflation (Mobile +20%, Laptop +8-10%), driving revenue but compressing blended gross margin (15.6% FY26 vs historical higher levels). Small Appliances: ~50% growth noted. Geography: Bihar (74% Q4 rev), UP (14%), Jharkhand (12%).
growth verticals / optionality: Deepening penetration in UP (only 30/75 districts covered); New state entry: Chhattisgarh (3 stores), Madhya Pradesh (planned FY27), and a previously withheld neighboring state now politically stable. Mature store mix improvement as >50% of stores cross 3-year mark.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin: 16% (Q4), 15.6% (FY26). EBITDA Margin: 8.1% (Q4), 8.5% (FY26). Pressure from low-margin high-ASP mobile/laptop mix. Operating expenses rose due to expansion freight, credit card commissions, and brand ambassador fees. Management expects opex to stabilize as new store % declines relative to mature base.
capex / expansion: Funded via internal accruals and working capital borrowings. No equity dilution planned. Spend directed toward new store openings (30+ run-rate) and strategic inventory buildup (INR 840cr).
capital allocation: Priority 1: New store openings in cluster approach. Priority 2: Strategic inventory procurement to hedge against OEM price hikes/supply shocks. Priority 3: Balance sheet strengthening. No dividends or buybacks highlighted; reinvestment mode.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk in new states (UP/MP/Chhattisgarh) vs Bihar maturity; Supply chain disruptions (Gulf war impact on gas/components); Real estate rental inflation (though currently stable in target regions); Margin recovery dependency on normalizing summer demand for cooling category.
management quality / tone: Confident and resilient. Emphasizes transition to 'all-weather' business model. Defensive on specific margin data (state-wise/mature vs new) citing competition, but clear on strategic intent to prioritize market share over short-term margin spikes during price hikes.
non-obvious takeaways: Inventory buildup (INR 840cr) is a deliberate arbitrage play on anticipated OEM price hikes (8-10%) and supply constraints, not just demand buffering. The 'weak' FY26 actually accelerated the maturity curve by forcing reliance on non-summer quarters, proving the H2 growth engine.

| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain constraints and raw material (gas) shortages leading to OEM price hikes | Voltas | beneficiary | Med | Aditya's strategic stocking indicates anticipated strong demand and price firmness in AC segment, benefiting manufacturers with pricing power. |
| Rural/semi-urban consumption recovery lagging in broader indices | Titan Company | beneficiary | Low | While Aditya focuses on durables, the confirmed rise in disposable income in Bihar/UP/Jharkhand supports broader discretionary spending, though direct correlation is weaker. |
| Intense competition in mobile/laptop segment compressing retailer margins | Vijaya Diagnostic Centre | loser | Low | Unrelated sector, but if consumer wallet share shifts heavily to high-ASP electronics due to inflation, discretionary health spend could face headwinds in these specific geographies. |

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.
themes.driver: Summer cooling demand; GST 2.0 price cuts; festive restocking; commodity-cost tailwind on margins; premiumization/ASP mix shift.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Incorporated in 1999 at Patna, the Company operates a brick-and-mortar, multi-brand retail chain selling televisions, air conditioners, refrigerators and washing machines, digital gadgets such as mobile phones and laptops, and personal care and kitchen appliances, to customers in urban centres and emerging Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets of the Hindi Heartland. As on March 31, 2026 it ran 207 stores with an average store size of 4,400+ sq. ft. and a retail footprint of ~9.1 lakh sq. ft. across Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. Retail trade of electronic products contributes 98.06% of turnover; customers are B2B and B2C, exports are nil, and the Company is not engaged in any production or manufacturing activity.

segment_detail.body: Cooling (AC/Coolers/Fridges): Margin dilution in H1 due to weak summer, expected recovery in H2/FY27. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Income infusion at the grassroots: ₹10,000 direct transfer to women in Bihar under Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana, ~1.30 crore beneficiaries and ₹13,000 Crore of liquidity injected, strengthening rural cash flows
- Structural household savings: free electricity up to 125 units/month in Bihar covering ~1.8 crore households under Mukhyamantri Vidyut Upbhokta Sahayata Yojana, worth ~₹900/month per household of recurring savings
- Pricing-led demand stimulus from GST 2.0 rationalization — tax reduction from 28% to 18% across key categories (ACs, dishwashers, TVs above 32 inches) and a ~7–8% reduction in retail prices
- Product-mix upgrade cycle from the BEE norm transition — shift toward 3-star and above appliances plus OEM discounting on outgoing inventory, driving replacement demand
- Credit-enabled consumption: strong growth in consumer financing and rising personal loan penetration across key markets
- Salary-led upside from the 8th Pay Commission, with a ~30–35% salary increase for government employees and pensioners lifting urban discretionary spending
- Diversified portfolio reduces seasonality — with summer categories soft in H1 FY26, washing machines, water purifiers and induction cooktops picked up, and H1 and H2 contributed almost evenly to annual performance
- Quarterly Y-O-Y growth accelerated through FY26 at 6%, 22%, 27% and 28%, delivering 18% topline growth despite the weakest summer in over two decades
- Industry backdrop: Indian consumer durables market valued at ₹6,240 Billion projected to grow at ~11% CAGR to ₹9,470 Billion by 2029, with shortening replacement cycles and service quality becoming a key retailer differentiator
- Watch-items flagged for the sector: commodity price volatility, an acute shortage of chips, and demand/supply impact from the ongoing Middle East crisis

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross Margin: 16% (Q4), 15.6% (FY26). EBITDA Margin: 8.1% (Q4), 8.5% (FY26). Pressure from low-margin high-ASP mobile/laptop mix. Operating expenses rose due to expansion freight, credit card commissions, and brand ambassador fees. Management expects opex to stabilize as new store % declines relative to mature base.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority 1: New store openings in cluster approach. Priority 2: Strategic inventory procurement to hedge against OEM price hikes/supply shocks. Priority 3: Balance sheet strengthening. No dividends or buybacks highlighted; reinvestment mode.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion for Aditya Vision is store roll-out, not plant capex. During FY26 the Company opened 32 new stores across four states — 6 in Bihar, 4 in Jharkhand, 19 in Uttar Pradesh and 3 in Chhattisgarh — crossing the milestone of 200 operational stores through focused, cluster-led expansion. As on March 31, 2026 the store count stands at 207: Bihar 118 (all 38 districts), Jharkhand 33 (22 of 24 districts), Uttar Pradesh 53 (30 of 75 districts) and Chhattisgarh 3 (2 of 33 districts); retail footprint rose 22% to 9,13,725 sq. ft. with an average store size of 4,400+ sq. ft. Under 'Strategic Growth Pillars and Future Outlook' the Company states it plans to add at least 25–30 stores annually over the next 2–3 years on the base of 207 stores, anchored in sustaining strong double-digit same-store sales growth. It is focused on deepening presence across Bihar, Jharkhand, Eastern, Central and Western Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, and on entering Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal in the current calendar year, targeting underpenetrated markets. Operations run on a cash-and-carry model with 100+ brand partnerships and real-time API integration enabling rapid replenishment; consumer-finance tie-ups include Bajaj Finserv, HDB Financial Services, IDFC First Bank, Paytm, Pine Labs, Samsung Finance+ and TVS Credit. The annual report states no rupee capex quantum for this expansion, and BRSR Principle 2 reports nil R&D and nil capex in technologies to improve environmental and social impacts in both the current and previous financial year.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and resilient. Emphasizes transition to 'all-weather' business model. Defensive on specific margin data (state-wise/mature vs new) citing competition, but clear on strategic intent to prioritize market share over short-term margin spikes during price hikes.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over 50% market share in Bihar and the largest electronics retailer in Jharkhand, giving regional dominance in underpenetrated markets
- 207 stores averaging 4,400+ sq. ft. and ~9.1 lakh sq. ft. of retail footprint across four states, built through prudent cluster-led expansion
- Physical retail model acts as a moat in regions where direct brand interaction remains critical
- Strong vendor partnerships and direct relationships with 100+ leading OEM brands, of which 85% of supply is direct OEM; no private labels
- Customer centricity through in-store experience, after-sales service (Aditya Seva) and access to flexible financing options
- Cash-and-carry model with low debt, controlled inventory and high cash reserves
- CRISIL Ratings reaffirmed 'CRISIL A/Stable' on long-term bank facilities in February 2026, citing established market position and sound operating efficiency

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution risk in new states (UP/MP/Chhattisgarh) vs Bihar maturity; Supply chain disruptions (Gulf war impact on gas/components); Real estate rental inflation (though currently stable in target regions); Margin recovery dependency on normalizing summer demand for cooling category.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Inventory buildup (INR 840cr) is a deliberate arbitrage play on anticipated OEM price hikes (8-10%) and supply constraints, not just demand buffering. The 'weak' FY26 actually accelerated the maturity curve by forcing reliance on non-summer quarters, proving the H2 growth engine.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain constraints and raw material (gas) shortages leading to OEM price hikes | Voltas | beneficiary | Med | Aditya's strategic stocking indicates anticipated strong demand and price firmness in AC segment, benefiting manufacturers with pricing power. |
| Rural/semi-urban consumption recovery lagging in broader indices | Titan Company | beneficiary | Low | While Aditya focuses on durables, the confirmed rise in disposable income in Bihar/UP/Jharkhand supports broader discretionary spending, though direct correlation is weaker. |
| Intense competition in mobile/laptop segment compressing retailer margins | Vijaya Diagnostic Centre | loser | Low | Unrelated sector, but if consumer wallet share shifts heavily to high-ASP electronics due to inflation, discretionary health spend could face headwinds in these specific geographies. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demand environment] Q1 FY27 demand was weather-split: 'East remained 5-8 degrees C cooler than North/Central during most of April & May', with Bihar and Jharkhand seeing intermittent rain and softer demand while UP's sustained heat supported cooling demand.
- [Consumer sentiment] Deck argues 'Sentiment, not income, became the key constraint', citing public messaging on gold read as a cue to 'Spend Less, Save More', LPG cylinder availability concerns, and a Rs 1,000 petrol pump purchase limit that led households to preserve cash.
- [Governance] Board is promoter-heavy at the executive level (Chairman & MD Yashovardhan Sinha, two promoter whole-time directors, two promoter non-executive directors) against six independent directors including ex-Samsung India and ex-UCO Bank veterans.
- [Demographics] Deck notes India's fertility has fallen below replacement (TFR 1.9) while its target states remain above it - Bihar 2.9, Uttar Pradesh 2.6, Madhya Pradesh 2.4, Chhattisgarh 2.2, Jharkhand 2.1.
